statements.status_notes: CVE-2011-3389 (BEAST) is a weakness of the CBC cipher suites in SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0, whose chained initialization vectors let a man-in-the-middle who can inject chosen plaintext into a client's connection recover parts of it: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2011-3389. GnuTLS has no mitigation for it in TLS 1.0, and Debian lists gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 in trixie as vulnerable with no fix, recommending TLS 1.1 or later. The built-in default priority of GnuTLS 3.8.9, the version this package ships, still includes TLS 1.0 (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/blob/3.8.9/lib/priority.c), so whether an application can negotiate it depends on its own priority string and its peer. Pending: a maintainer decision on whether to publish this owner as AFFECTED with no fixed version, or as NOT_AFFECTED on a reason that holds for every image that uses it.
